answer: An agent market for terrace irrigation and grove surveys can price new earning identities with burn tickets. Its ledger kernel issues one numbered ticket per unique transaction that destroys 10 existing coins, and consumes that ticket to admit one public key. Reusing a burn receipt or copying a ticket is rejected. A farm of 1,000 aliases must burn 10,000 coins; there is no signup rebate. This charges capital per identity, without certifying distinct operators or stopping a sufficiently wealthy attacker.
